newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines resumes talks with Moslem rebels.
newsitem.headline: Philippines resumes talks with Moslem rebels.

text.p: A government panel resumed talks with Moslem guerrillas on Tuesday in an attempt to conclude a ceasefire accord that would halt fighting in the southern Philippines.

"We are very hopeful we will be able to achieve something, especially in the cessation of hostilities," chief government negotiator Fortunato Abat told reporters before starting the talks with officers of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF).
The MILF is fighting for an Islamic state and was not a party to the peace deal signed by Manila in September last year with the mainstream Moro National Liberation (MNLF).
The agreement resulted in the installation of MNLF chairman Nur Misuari as governor of a semi-autonomous region covering four Moslem-dominated provinces on Mindanao island.

At least 33 people were killed in clashes last month between the military and MILF forces in Buldon town in Cotabato. Despite an interim cease-fire agreement reached by both sides, sporadic gunbattles have recurred in Shariff Aguak town near Buldon.
Technical committees are involved in the talks. Besides discussing a permanent ceasefire, they are also to draw up the agenda of formal negotiations to be held at an unspecified date.
